details:
**"Many years later, as he faced the firing squad..."**
The famous opening line of the novel: "Many years later, as he faced the firing squad, Colonel Aureliano Buendia was to remember that distant afternoon when his father took him to discover ice." The ice is shown in the tent of the gypsies, and the father mistakes it for a giant diamond. This is the single most common late clue and giveaway.

**Melquiades and his manuscripts**
The leader of a band of gypsies who visits Macondo each year, bringing wonders like magnets, a giant magnifying glass, daguerreotypes, flying carpets, and ice. He leaves behind parchments written in Sanskrit that foretell the family's entire history. At the novel's end, Aureliano Babilonia deciphers them just as a whirlwind wipes Macondo off the earth.

**Child born with a pig's tail**
The incest the family has always feared finally produces a baby with a pig's tail, born to Amaranta Ursula and her nephew Aureliano Babilonia. Amaranta Ursula dies after the birth, and the neglected infant (named Aureliano) is carried off and eaten by ants, fulfilling the prophecy in Melquiades's manuscripts.

**Jose Arcadio Buendia tied to the chestnut tree**
The family patriarch and founder of Macondo becomes obsessed with science and alchemy, then goes mad (believing every day is Monday after failing to build a perpetual motion machine). He speaks only in Latin, so his family ties him to a chestnut tree in the courtyard, where he spends his final years. At his death, a rain of tiny yellow flowers falls on the town.

**Seventeen sons named Aureliano and the Ash Wednesday crosses**
During the civil wars, Colonel Aureliano Buendia fathers seventeen sons by seventeen different women, all named Aureliano. When they visit, Father Antonio Isabel marks them with Ash Wednesday crosses that never wash off. Government assassins later use the crosses as targets and shoot the brothers in the forehead.

**Banana company massacre and the train of corpses**
Striking workers at the American banana company are machine-gunned by soldiers in the town square. Jose Arcadio Segundo wakes up on a train carrying thousands of corpses ("man corpses, woman corpses, child corpses") to be dumped in the sea. Afterward, nobody else remembers the massacre, and it rains for nearly five years, washing away its memory. The episode is based on the real 1928 banana massacre in Colombia.

**Remedios the Beauty ascends to heaven**
A woman so beautiful that several men die because of their desire for her. One afternoon, while folding sheets in the garden, she suddenly rises into the sky and disappears, taking the sheets with her.

**Colonel Aureliano Buendia and his little gold fishes**
The family's most famous son leads 32 failed liberal uprisings and ends the war by signing the Treaty of Neerlandia (the real treaty that ended Colombia's War of the Thousand Days). He shoots himself in the chest through a circle of iodine his doctor painted, but survives; at that moment Ursula finds a pot of milk full of worms. In old age he withdraws to his workshop to make little gold fishes, melting them down and remaking them endlessly.

**Mauricio Babilonia and the yellow butterflies**
A mechanic who is always surrounded by yellow butterflies and who becomes the secret lover of Meme. Her mother, Fernanda del Carpio, has a guard posted, and Mauricio is shot in the spine as a supposed chicken thief, leaving him paralyzed. Meme falls silent for the rest of her life and is sent to a convent, where she gives birth to their son, Aureliano Babilonia.

**Rebeca, the dirt-eating orphan, and the insomnia plague**
Rebeca arrives at the Buendia house carrying a canvas bag of her parents' bones and a rocking chair, and she secretly eats only earth and whitewash. She brings with her an insomnia plague that spreads through Macondo and causes people to lose their memories, forcing them to label every object with its name.

**Pietro Crespi**
An Italian pianola technician and music teacher who becomes engaged to Rebeca, then courts her adoptive sister Amaranta after Rebeca marries Jose Arcadio. When Amaranta rejects him, he cuts his wrists. Amaranta later wears a black bandage on her hand for the rest of her life and dies a virgin.

**Ursula Iguaran and the fear of incest**
The matriarch who lives for over a century and holds the family together. She is the cousin of her husband Jose Arcadio Buendia and fears their children will be born with pig's tails, so she refuses to consummate the marriage. He replies, "If you have iguanas, we'll raise iguanas."

**Prudencio Aguilar and the founding of Macondo**
After losing a cockfight to Jose Arcadio Buendia, Prudencio Aguilar mocks him about his unconsummated marriage. Jose Arcadio Buendia kills him with a spear, and Prudencio's ghost, with a wound in his throat, haunts him. To escape it the couple leaves Riohacha, and Jose Arcadio Buendia founds Macondo on a riverbank after dreaming of a city with walls of mirrors.

**Father Nicanor levitates**
A priest who drinks a cup of hot chocolate and then rises several inches off the ground to prove the existence of God, so he can raise money to build a church. The mad Jose Arcadio Buendia, speaking Latin, dismisses it as merely a "fourth state of matter."

**Aureliano Segundo, Petra Cotes, and the eating contest**
Petra Cotes is a concubine whose lovemaking makes the livestock of her lover Aureliano Segundo multiply fantastically. At first she doesn't realize she is sleeping with both him and his look-alike twin Jose Arcadio Segundo. Aureliano Segundo nearly dies in an eating contest against a woman called "the Elephant."
